children: Walt Disney is raising its streaming subscription prices for the second time in a year as it looks to focus on investing in content.

Certain plans' prices will rise by as much as 10%. The move comes at a notable time: The popularity of Meta Platform's Muse has raised concerns that artificial-intelligence agents pose risks to companies that rely on recurring payments s if they help consumers cancel those payments from simple prompts.
A Disney spokesperson confirmed the price changes to Barron's on Wednesday.

"We continue to significantly invest in enhancements to Disney+-new technology, features, and personalization. These improvements continue to strengthen the value we deliver to subscribers and will culminate in the one app experience later this year," the spokesperson said.

Disney is raising the price for its ad-free Disney+ and Hulu bundle by $2, or 10%, to $21.99. The price for the Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN Select Bundle with ads is also increasing by $2 to $21.99, while the ad-free Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Select Bundle is increasing by $3 to $32.99.
Disney is keeping the price of its Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads at $12.99. The company also isn't changing the price of the Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle Premium plan at $44.99.

Other streaming services have taken similar steps this year. Netflix raised its prices in March while Comcast's Peacock raised its prices in August. Disney last raised prices for its streaming plans in October 2025.

It's an interesting time for Disney to boost prices. This week, a major conversation on Wall Street has been about AI agents' possible impact on companies that rely on so-called "consumer inertia." That's the idea that consumers will continue to pay for products and services on a recurring basis because its easier than canceling those subscriptions or looking for alternatives.

For instance, Meta Platforms' AI agent Muse, which launched earlier this month, can complete tasks for a user, like looking through that person's email, finding subscriptions, and canceling them. It takes minimal effort from the user and could lead to cancellations of ongoing recurring payments. That could pose a risk for streaming services like Disney+ and Netflix.
Disney and Netflix stock both fell on Tuesday and Wednesday as these worries mounted.

Disney stock was down 0.5% to $103.31 on Wednesday while the S&P 500 declined 0.7%. Shareholders will surely be watching how far these companies can take these price increases, especially as AI agents make it easier than ever for consumers to step away.
